key_insight: Lead-free double perovskites K/Rb2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be thermodynamically stable, mechanically ductile, and composition-tunable from wide-gap photovoltaics to low-gap optoelectronics and thermoelectrics.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a scalable, non-toxic candidate platform for solar absorbers, tandem/NIR devices, and waste-heat recovery with strong thermal-process tolerance.
method: DFT evaluation of structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Stability screening using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Band structure and transport analysis across Cl/Br/I substitutions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds as stable cubic phases with direct bandgaps tuned from 1.44 to 0.64 eV and a peak predicted ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions only, so experimental synthesis, phase purity, and real-device performance still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
